correctness.rationale: All matching simplices are exhaustively regenerated: augmented f-vector (1,12,42,44,9). Exact F2 boundary ranks (1,11,31,9), signed integer boundary-square cancellations and rank upper bounds force rational reduced homology only in degree 2 with dimension 4. For each of all 48 affine cube symmetries signed fixed-matching traces yield epsilon+sign(pi)(fixed diagonals-1); 10 rational character inner products are integral and identify exactly epsilon and the inflated S^(2,1,1) module. Fixed-group invariants then determine the rational quotient homology. The runnable verifier reproduces each finite calculation; no unproved higher-parameter generalization is used.

originality.rationale: The identical cube ordinary matching complex is already known to be a wedge of four two-spheres (record 79d70fe8b67e), but its full 48-element rational homology representation does not follow from that homotopy classification. Relevant grid and matching-complex primary texts, all nearby result records, and aliases were compared. Neither dual-octahedral matching representations nor cube 3-cut representations determine this ordinary matching module. Unindexed equivalent work remains a genuine residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently titled earlier calculation may contain the same full cube matching homology representation.
There is no independent external referee validation; only finite internal checks and full-text comparisons are claimed.

value.rationale: The full action of the canonical 48-element cube symmetry group on a natural four-dimensional matching-homology module is a meaningful invariant distinct from the known sphere count. The theorem determines how central inversion divides its homology (three even and one odd dimension) and establishes two rational orbit-space homology classifications. These consequences address symmetry of the precise canonical object, not an arbitrary parameter slice; the limited rational finite-object scope is explicit.
